## 1. Define a term before you use it, and use plain words everywhere else

A reader new to the repository has only the skill, its brief and its training. A word with a meaning that the record gave it (a defect's "home", a "stop" that does not stop, "corpus") tells it nothing or the wrong thing. Where its training holds a near thing, name it ("as LLVM's lit does"): one clause corrects an assumption where a paragraph would not.
- Marked: "In every report, give each defect's home, ..."
- Accepted: "In your report, list each defect that you found, with the test or ledger row that records it."

## 2. Put the concepts first, as a dictionary, then the procedures in the order that the work meets them

A chain of do's and don'ts cannot be held in mind; a concept named once (an area, building, exploring, a point to report) makes each procedure short and tells the reader when to switch. A glossary entry is the term, then a noun phrase with no article. A comment marks a problem area: fix it at its paragraph or section, with the whole skill in mind.
- Marked: "- The base is the commit that your work starts from."
- Accepted: "**base**" / ": Commit that your work starts from."

## 3. Every sentence tells the reader what to do or a fact it needs to do it; cut the rest

Every agent pays for every token, and a sentence that changes nothing hides the ones that do: a slogan (a decision's title copied from the record), a step the agent takes anyway, a rule it cannot act on, a rule against a failure that never happened, a rule its system prompt gives, a back reference, a provenance word.
- Marked: "1. Read your brief. 2. Load the parts below that your task touches. [...] 4. Do the work."
- Accepted: "Load the parts below that your task touches before you run the query of the record that your brief gives. The parts give the words [...]"

## 4. State a rule for exactly the cases where it holds, and bound it to the agent's brief and its own work

An absolute ("never wipe the caches") is wrong in the cases it did not name. Authority reaches an agent through its brief alone, and what a role or a workflow does belongs there, not in the skill.
- Marked: "Before you build or run something, look for its result on record. If the record or another agent's transcript holds the result [...], cite that result"
- Accepted: "Reuse each result of a build, a suite, a stage of the gate or a test that your brief cites or that your own work ran. Cite it."

Misapplied: cutting the default for a silent brief ("If it says nothing, commit your own files as you go") leaves the agent with no action. A cut never removes a default.

## 5. Say what to do, in the positive, one instruction per sentence, the condition first; add a reason only where it helps judge a case the rule does not name

- Accepted: "When you probe or debug, change one thing at a time, so that each result has one cause."

## 7. Put knowledge in the part loaded when it is needed; name a note only with a trigger and a narrow read

So the part holds what daily work needs, and a note it names comes with when to open it and the query that prints the slice. <!-- The baseline interview: a setting and eighteen questions that a fresh session of a model answers with its default instincts for the coordinator's job (where it keeps the project's memory, what it does with a worker's report, how it talks to the curator on a phone, how it decides and delegates), run in a private namespace with no record, no skill and no tool, so that the `coordinator` skill can be written to hold only what the model would not do by itself; kept so that it is run again for each new model, Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 first, 2026-10-12, at the curator's word. -->

# The baseline interview

The `coordinator` skill is written on one principle, the curator's: it holds only what the model would not do by itself. What is specific to this project (the nine steps, test first under the sealed tree, the gate) and what is specific to this environment (the curator reads on a phone and dictates, the context is compacted, the container can be lost, the curator decides) go in. A rule that restates the model's own default is left out.

The baseline is what a model does by default. This kit finds it by interview, not by replay: a fresh session gets the setting and the questions, and nothing else, and answers with its instinct. An interview shows what a model says it would do, not what it does; the curator accepted that limit when he chose the method (POSITIONS, "The coordinator rewrite's goals").

## The files

- `setting.md`: the situation and the constraints the session is given. It names none of the record's files or terms, so that it does not prime the answer.
- `questions.md`: eighteen questions in four groups, memory and reports, talking to the curator, decisions, workers and runs. They follow the six groups of conduct rules in `process-engineering/coordinator-shape.md`, section 4.1, so that every rule can meet a default.
- `run.sh`: runs one model's interview. Its header says how the session is isolated.
- `answers/<model>.md`: each model's answers, verbatim, with the date, the Claude Code version and the effort at the top. The model is named by its version name, never by its identifier.

## How to run it

    explorations/coordinator/baseline-interview/run.sh fable /tmp/interview/fable
    explorations/coordinator/baseline-interview/run.sh opus  /tmp/interview/opus

The out-dir must lie outside `/home/user` and `/root`. Copy `answer.md` to `answers/<model>.md` with the header lines from `meta.txt`, the model's version name in place of its id. Each run writes under 0.1M tokens.

## How the answers are used

The conduct rules of the protocol and POSITIONS are sorted against the answers into three buckets: a default the model gives by itself (deleted), an environment rule (kept) and a project rule (kept). The skill is written from the two kept buckets.

## When to run it again

When a new model is to take the coordinating session, run the interview for it before the skill is adjusted, and keep its answers beside the others. The questions change only when the environment or the project changes what the coordinator must do; a changed question is run again for every model whose answers are kept.

1	<!-- A review of the coordinator skill's outline (`coordinator-skill-outline.md`), written 2026-10-13 by a Fable reviewer for the curator: the placements checked against the entries, what is wrong or missing with its fix, the outline as the writer should get it, what the writer's brief and the plan's decisions change, and what the curator sees in the morning. -->
2	
3	# The outline reviewed: right in shape, four placements to change
4	
5	The outline is right in its shape. A core of seven sections and six parts match the five roles, the curator's three rulings and the plan's candidates. Every entry of FACTS and POSITIONS that leaves has a home, and every point of the held list on how we work has one. I found no part that should not exist and no part that is missing. I found three project decisions moved out that should stay in part, one fact of state put in the skill, three kept rules with no home, two rules with two homes, one held point in the wrong part, and one timing that would leave the coordinator without its rules for five steps. The fixes are small. The writer can run tonight on the outline with the changes in section 3.
6	
7	Line numbers are the outline's, at commit `77ab93037`. Nothing has touched FACTS or POSITIONS since, so they are current (`git log 77ab93037..HEAD` on the two files is empty). Times are UTC.
8	
9	## 1. What I checked
10	
11	- Every borderline entry of section 2.3 and every split entry of section 2.4, read whole: POSITIONS 8, 14, 19, 27, 31, 32, 33, 39, 61, 87, 123, 124, 125, 132, 133, 135, 136; FACTS 66, 111, 190, 192, 203, 219.
12	- The two conduct sections of POSITIONS whole (lines 100 to 145) and the container section of FACTS whole (lines 189 to 215). That covers the ten others and more: 102 to 122, 126 to 131, 134, 140 to 145; FACTS 189, 191, 193 to 202, 204 to 215.
13	- The "already there" claims that the placements rest on, by grep in the named parts: `session.md` (the 270 s cap, the permission check), `committing.md` ("What to commit", "Pushing"), `exploring.md` ("The choices that are yours"), `interpreter.md` (the order that varies run to run), `tests-writing.md` ("Names, comments, citations", refusals at load), `build-and-caches.md` ("Setting up each call", the `rats` folders), `worktrees.md` (seeding), `gate.md` ("When to run it"), `records.md` (read whole), `cloud-container`'s `hooks.md` and `machine.md`. All hold. `gate.md` names neither the checker-count stage nor what a comparison masks, so those are new pieces, as the outline says.
14	- The held list whole, the plan whole, both sorts, and the Opus answers of the baseline interview.
15	
16	## 2. What is wrong or missing
17	
18	Each point gives the evidence and the fix.
19	
20	1. **Two project decisions on the suites leave whole.** POSITIONS 103, "The suite's verdict is the check.", decides what a test holds: a value that matters is asserted, no expected-output files, and "none of it is offered to him again". POSITIONS 102, "Test first, the test kept.", decides how the tree is changed: a failing test first, kept in the corpus, test and fix in one commit. The outline keeps 124 and 125 because they decide what the suites hold and how they run (section 2.3). 102 and 103 are decisions of the same kind, on the same suites. They are not "working between us". The worker rules are already in `fortress-repo` (`SKILL.md`, "Rules for every task"; `tests-writing.md`). Fix: both leave in part. 102 keeps its first sentence and the one-commit sentence; the skeptic's reading of test-first from the transcript goes to Part 2. 103 keeps its first sentence and "no expected-output files; none of it is offered to him again"; "no batch compares the corpus's printed outputs, no baseline is run" goes to Part 2. Both stay in the project section the outline proposes, "The suites and the gate".
21	2. **A decision on the gate's stages leaves whole.** POSITIONS 39, "The checker count is measured, never red.", decides that a gate stage is a measurement and that the phase-3 gates' job is driving the distance down. The outline's own definition of the project (section 2.1) names "the gate's stages as measurements". `fortress-repo` holds nothing of these stages, by POSITIONS 134, so after the move only FACTS 66 would say that the total is never red, and a fact is not his decision. Fix: 39 stays where it is, in "The one library and the compiled checker". Part 2 cites it and holds the batch's handling: `STAGE_BLIND`, the before tables, the review's tie of each risen row to a rung edit. Section 2.5 then reads 25 of 26.
22	3. **A fact of state goes into the core.** Core 4 would say "the coordinating session runs on Opus, and moves to Fable at his word" (POSITIONS 117). The entry itself says the tier changes at his word, and it changed on 10-12. A skill line of state goes stale at the first switch, and the boot note is the one home of state (HELD 42, decision 20). Fix: Core 4 states the tiers, that the session's tier is his to set, and his two reasons (the register, the pool). The current tier is a line of the boot note.
23	4. **Three kept rules have no home.** The plan's kept list (section 3, point 6) keeps "Give reading to workers. Read their reports and the record." (its failure: the repository traced by hand on 09-19), "No directory listings at boot, and every output bounded" (decision 7, kept by default), and "A go is written nowhere" (the half of "A remark isn't a decision"). None of the three appears in the outline's sections 1.1 or 1.2. They come from the protocol, not from an entry, so section 2.2 has no line for them, and the core's lines "A remark is not a decision" and "Weigh a rule by its purpose and its cost" have the same gap. Fix: Core 1 adds delegation, beside the standing goal: the coordinator's context is for him and the record; reading and long work go to workers. Core 6 adds the bounded boot. Core 2's remark line adds "a go is written nowhere". Section 1 says once that the protocol's conduct rules land by the plan's kept list, and names them where they land.
24	5. **Two rules have two homes.** The Workflow's mechanics (FACTS 201, 208, 209) are listed under Part 1 and Part 2 (section 2.7), and "what belongs in which skill" stands in Core 5 and in Part 5. The plan's rule is one home per thing. Fix: Part 1 holds the mechanics; Part 2 says when a batch resumes and points to Part 1. Core 5 holds the skills' split; Part 5 points to it.
25	6. **One held point is in the wrong part.** HELD 80, "Unsure about PLAN.md, the big plan file, as the place", is sent to Part 3 as "what PLAN holds". Its context (HELD 73 to 81) is the ledger's regrouping proposal, and "the place" is PLAN as the home of the regrouped rows. Fix: Part 4, beside HELD 81 (no go on re-deriving the views).
26	7. **The evicted entries leave POSITIONS too early.** Section 3.2, point 2, sends them to the history once the skill holds them and the check against the kept list (step 7) has read them. From step 7 to step 12 the coordinator still boots on the old skill and the protocol and reads POSITIONS whole; the new skill is not in use until his reading is done and the old homes are retired. For those five steps the conduct rules would be in no file the boot reads. Fix: the evicted entries leave with the protocol at step 12, "Retire the old homes", each to `POSITIONS-history.md` with one line naming its home. Decision 17 changes with it (section 4).
27	8. **One entry's fate is left open.** POSITIONS 61, "The separate analysis session's scope.", goes to Part 1 "if that session is over, to the history instead". Neither BOOT nor PLAN names such a session now. Fix: Part 1 holds the general rule, a second session contributes reviews and their commits on a branch of its own, not a batch or a change of route. The entry goes to the history. The consolidation checks whether the session still runs before it does.
28	9. **A fact about the original tree would leave FACTS.** FACTS 192 holds the leak's mechanism with its file and lines (`RatsUtil.java:138-145`, 5.8 MB each, never deleted) and sends the whole entry out on the strength of row 702. Fix: a check, not a move. Before the entry leaves, the consolidation reads row 702. If the row holds the mechanism with its lines, the entry leaves as the outline says. If not, the first two sentences stay as a FACTS entry of the tree.
29	10. **Section 3.3 misses four decisions the outline changes.** It names decision 23 only. Decisions 6, 17, 18 and 22 change too (section 4 below).
30	11. **Point 2 of the writer's brief contradicts the outline.** It gives the writer POSITIONS's conduct sections "as consolidated". The outline's section 3.2, point 2, does not rewrite them. Fix: "as they stand".
31	
32	What I did not check: the README's rule sections, PLAN's three old rule sections and the boot note's standing lines. They are outside the outline's scope. The map's section 4.1 gives each of their rules its lines, and the kept list covers them. Step 12 retires them against that map.
33	
34	## 3. The outline as the writer should get it
35	
36	The outline's section 1 stands with the changes below folded in. Its section 2 is the map of homes, with the changed placements listed at the end of this section. The sizes are the plan's: the core about 10K bytes, the whole skill no longer than 41K bytes, the sources file aside. The protocol's conduct rules land by the plan's kept list; they are named below where they land.
37	
38	### 3.1 The core
39	
40	Loaded at every session start and after every compaction. It holds what bears on any turn.
41	
42	1. **The standing goal.** Model what he knows and where his gaps are. Fill them with the few facts he needs to decide. Do not re-explain what he knows. The two hats. The coordinator's context is for him and the record: reading and long work go to workers, and the coordinator reads their reports. The profile of what he knows, once built, is read here.
43	2. **His role and his decisions.** He sets the goals and decides the design and process questions put to him. A bare go starts background work only; a batch needs his explicit go; a standing go covers what it names. What makes a decision consequential, and its three ways to him. A decision inside a worker's report is not made until he sees it. Search the record before asking him or measuring. A remark is not a decision, and a go is written nowhere. A deeper pass, not a halt or a rollback. Weigh a rule by its purpose and its cost. The coordinator's own proposal stays marked as its own until his yes. Any Fable worker beyond the standing pre-approvals needs his yes.
44	3. **Talking to him.** The register. The ask: what the work does, produces, touches and costs, what a yes commits him to and what a no costs; one ask per message, in the context its text gives; the recommendation last, in a line. Lists, not tables. Numbers as K or M, few, each with its meaning. A new term defined where it is used. A choice numbered. No dialog tool, a rule that lapses with the client. Time read from the clock, given in UTC and his time. Costs in tokens, writes only. Silence while a batch runs. Record edits: decision 11. The hook's reminders handled silently. While he reads turn by turn, restate each point in a line and hold it until he is done. No do-nothing option among the choices. Pages for him: a Select button per section, sources at the bottom, the house style, updated by URL after a compaction, a lost source rebuilt from the page. A push notification when he is away. A position's bold title is the record's handle, never quoted as his words.
45	4. **The facts of this environment.** His iPhone, Speak and dictation. A path does not open there; a page link or a GitHub URL does. His client can show stale state; the tree is the truth. His time zone. Compaction. A lost container keeps only what is pushed. Auto mode, the permission check and manual mode. The caches' lives: an hour for the session and a headless session, five minutes for a subagent. The platform's process stops. A message during a turn is queued; a stop kills the running agents. Cached reads are almost free. The tiers: workers on Opus, archaeology on Sonnet, Fable for a two-area judgement and the pre-approved reviews. The session's tier is his to set, for the register and the pool; the current tier is the boot note's.
46	5. **The record: what goes where.** Each home and its purpose: FACTS and POSITIONS (the project only, read in briefs), the history files, INDEX, PLAN, the boot note (the one home of state), the held list, the review queue, the notes and reports, the gap ledger, and the skills (how we work: this skill; rules that bind workers: `fortress-repo`; the platform: `cloud-container`). One home per thing. What he says about how we work comes here, refined. Push after every commit.
47	6. **The boot.** The boot order. What is read whole and what is looked up, which the trial boot settles. No directory listings; every output bounded. What is in flight, read from the tree. Whether a worker still runs: the harness's notice and its one output path. `git log`, one line. The boot note rewritten whole. After each start of the process, the git-check hook's reset, told to him in a line.
48	7. **The parts.** One line for each part: what it holds and when to load it.
49	
50	### 3.2 The parts
51	
52	Each is loaded when the coordinator switches into its work. Several can be loaded at once. No part restates another; it points.
53	
54	1. **Delegating: briefing, launching, watching and resuming agents.** The briefer of workers. Loaded before the coordinator briefs, launches, watches, resumes or relaunches any agent, a batch's agents included. It holds the tiers, the Fable rule and the all-models pool; what a brief holds (the problem and not the answer, the research on file, the record's measurements as findings, the record's slice quoted and not restated, a length cap for an update, no second reader that reframes a document, no request that a worker cap its own spend, his rule quoted and never restated); watching a long run against its estimate, with check-ins armed at launch; waits and the prompt cache; interrupts and stops of the process; the Workflow's mechanics as their one home (a run resumed with the same script and arguments, a copy of the script as launched, the journal; `agent()` returning null; the async-body check); relaunching only at his ask; headless sessions; the scope of a second session (reviews on its own branch, not a batch or a change of route); a worker that builds a page pointed to the house CSS.
55	2. **Running and reviewing a batch.** The batch coordinator. Loaded when a batch is prepared, launched, watched, landed or reviewed. It holds the go a batch needs and the standing go's sequence; the workflow script and its manual, in scope for improvement; the base built once and the seeded worktrees; the roles (worker, skeptic, judge) and what each checks, the skeptic's reading of test-first from the transcript among them; no batch comparison of outputs and no baseline run; reversible stops, the blocking second review, tests-only repairs, and a deeper pass on a red gate; what a batch commits; the mission briefing; the checker-count and distance stages, citing POSITIONS "The checker count is measured, never red.", with `STAGE_BLIND` and the before tables; every masked difference and respelled line listed for him; the landing (consolidation, `revival-changes.md` updated, items listed for him); the review after every batch; when a batch resumes after a stop or the limits, pointing to Part 1 for how.

57	4. **Keeping the record.** The record-keeping part of the plan's step 2, with the record store's tool if he takes it. Loaded when the coordinator edits FACTS, POSITIONS, INDEX or a history file, folds a worker's report into the record, or runs a consolidation. It holds an entry's form and measure; the numbered entries; the history and its provenance; the pass after a worker finishes; the consolidation and its checks (nothing lost, the length check or a reader's, the quiz); INDEX's lines; the ledger as one file with derived views, its rows numbered for good, written only with `ledger.py`, a rewrite split among small workers after a duplicate search; a record that is public and names models on purpose. 59	6. **Analysis: process engineering and post-mortems.** The analyst. Loaded when the coordinator measures what the work costs or how long it takes, tests a change to the process, or finds out what happened and why. It holds where the work's costs are measured; the spend read from the transcripts' usage records; a boot's cost and the tokens per byte; the Fable ratio; the development loop as a first-class concern; small tests on the records at hand; archaeology by Sonnet scouts; reading transcripts and Workflow journals; the post-mortem's index into a transcript; the profile of what he knows, built here as its own task; the open experiments he named (HELD 108, 113, 115, 118).
60	
61	### 3.3 The placements changed from the note
62	
63	1. POSITIONS 102, "Test first, the test kept.": leaves in part. Stays: the first sentence and the one-commit sentence, in "The suites and the gate". Leaves: the skeptic's reading from the transcript, to Part 2. The worker rule is already in `tests-writing.md`.

67	5. POSITIONS 61, "The separate analysis session's scope.": Part 1 as the general rule; the entry to the history after the consolidation's check.
68	6. HELD 80: Part 4, not Part 3.
69	7. Core 1 adds delegation, from the protocol.
70	8. Core 6 adds the bounded boot, from the protocol (decision 7).
71	9. Core 2 adds "a go is written nowhere", from the protocol.
72	10. FACTS 201, 208 and 209: Part 1 only. Part 2 points.

81	
82	- **Point 2.** The rule texts are POSITIONS's two conduct sections as they stand, not as consolidated; the protocol; the 3 entries and 5 clauses that leave POSITIONS from other sections, with the clauses of 102 and 103; the 2 FACTS clauses; the 26 container entries and the ledger entry; and the held list's 23 rules and 32 questions, each with its home. 85	- **Point 5.** The shape is the outline's section 1: a core of seven sections and six parts, no part restating another.

99	- **Decision 23, FACTS's container section.** Default flipped, as the outline says: move, by its homes; the coordinator's entries at step 6, the platform's at step 13.
100	- **New, from this review.** Three of his decisions stay in POSITIONS in part (102, 103) or whole (39). Default: yes. They are his decisions' homes, so he sees it.
101	
102	## 5. What the curator sees in the morning
103	
104	1. The three decisions that stay in POSITIONS in part or whole (102, 103, 39), one ask, default yes.
105	2. Decision 17's new default: the conduct entries leave POSITIONS at step 12, with the protocol.
106	3. The container section leaving FACTS (decision 23 flipped), and decision 18's default reworded.
107	4. The current tier of the coordinating session moved to the boot note.

# The outline reviewed: right in shape, four placements to change

The outline is right in its shape. A core of seven sections and six parts match the five roles, the curator's three rulings and the plan's candidates. Every entry of FACTS and POSITIONS that leaves has a home, and every point of the held list on how we work has one. I found no part that should not exist and no part that is missing. I found three project decisions moved out that should stay in part, one fact of state put in the skill, three kept rules with no home, two rules with two homes, one held point in the wrong part, and one timing that would leave the coordinator without its rules for five steps. The fixes are small. The writer can run tonight on the outline with the changes in section 3.

Line numbers are the outline's, at commit `77ab93037`. Nothing has touched FACTS or POSITIONS since, so they are current (`git log 77ab93037..HEAD` on the two files is empty). Times are UTC.

## 1. What I checked

- Every borderline entry of section 2.3 and every split entry of section 2.4, read whole: POSITIONS 8, 14, 19, 27, 31, 32, 33, 39, 61, 87, 123, 124, 125, 132, 133, 135, 136; FACTS 66, 111, 190, 192, 203, 219.

- The held list whole, the plan whole, both sorts, and the Opus answers of the baseline interview.

## 2. What is wrong or missing

Each point gives the evidence and the fix.

1. **Two project decisions on the suites leave whole.** POSITIONS 103, "The suite's verdict is the check.", decides what a test holds: a value that matters is asserted, no expected-output files, and "none of it is offered to him again". POSITIONS 102, "Test first, the test kept.", decides how the tree is changed: a failing test first, kept in the corpus, test and fix in one commit. The outline keeps 124 and 125 because they decide what the suites hold and how they run (section 2.3). 102 and 103 are decisions of the same kind, on the same suites. They are not "working between us". The worker rules are already in `fortress-repo` (`SKILL.md`, "Rules for every task"; `tests-writing.md`). Fix: both leave in part. 102 keeps its first sentence and the one-commit sentence; the skeptic's reading of test-first from the transcript goes to Part 2. 103 keeps its first sentence and "no expected-output files; none of it is offered to him again"; "no batch compares the corpus's printed outputs, no baseline is run" goes to Part 2. Both stay in the project section the outline proposes, "The suites and the gate".
2. **A decision on the gate's stages leaves whole.** POSITIONS 39, "The checker count is measured, never red.", decides that a gate stage is a measurement and that the phase-3 gates' job is driving the distance down. The outline's own definition of the project (section 2.1) names "the gate's stages as measurements". `fortress-repo` holds nothing of these stages, by POSITIONS 134, so after the move only FACTS 66 would say that the total is never red, and a fact is not his decision. Fix: 39 stays where it is, in "The one library and the compiled checker". Part 2 cites it and holds the batch's handling: `STAGE_BLIND`, the before tables, the review's tie of each risen row to a rung edit. Section 2.5 then reads 25 of 26.
3. **A fact of state goes into the core.** Core 4 would say "the coordinating session runs on Opus, and moves to Fable at his word" (POSITIONS 117). The entry itself says the tier changes at his word, and it changed on 10-12. A skill line of state goes stale at the first switch, and the boot note is the one home of state (HELD 42, decision 20). Fix: Core 4 states the tiers, that the session's tier is his to set, and his two reasons (the register, the pool). The current tier is a line of the boot note.
4. **Three kept rules have no home.** The plan's kept list (section 3, point 6) keeps "Give reading to workers. Read their reports and the record." (its failure: the repository traced by hand on 09-19), "No directory listings at boot, and every output bounded" (decision 7, kept by default), and "A go is written nowhere" (the half of "A remark isn't a decision"). None of the three appears in the outline's sections 1.1 or 1.2. They come from the protocol, not from an entry, so section 2.2 has no line for them, and the core's lines "A remark is not a decision" and "Weigh a rule by its purpose and its cost" have the same gap. Fix: Core 1 adds delegation, beside the standing goal: the coordinator's context is for him and the record; reading and long work go to workers. Core 6 adds the bounded boot. Core 2's remark line adds "a go is written nowhere". Section 1 says once that the protocol's conduct rules land by the plan's kept list, and names them where they land.
5. **Two rules have two homes.** The Workflow's mechanics (FACTS 201, 208, 209) are listed under Part 1 and Part 2 (section 2.7), and "what belongs in which skill" stands in Core 5 and in Part 5. The plan's rule is one home per thing. Fix: Part 1 holds the mechanics; Part 2 says when a batch resumes and points to Part 1. Core 5 holds the skills' split; Part 5 points to it.
6. **One held point is in the wrong part.** HELD 80, "Unsure about PLAN.md, the big plan file, as the place", is sent to Part 3 as "what PLAN holds". For those five steps the conduct rules would be in no file the boot reads. Fix: the evicted entries leave with the protocol at step 12, "Retire the old homes", each to `POSITIONS-history.md` with one line naming its home. Decision 17 changes with it (section 4).

The entry goes to the history. The consolidation checks whether the session still runs before it does.

Fix: a check, not a move. Before the entry leaves, the consolidation reads row 702. If the row holds the mechanism with its lines, the entry leaves as the outline says. 10. **Section 3.3 misses four decisions the outline changes.** It names decision 23 only. Decisions 6, 17, 18 and 22 change too (section 4 below).

## 3. The outline as the writer should get it

The outline's section 1 stands with the changes below folded in. Its section 2 is the map of homes, with the changed placements listed at the end of this section. The sizes are the plan's: the core about 10K bytes, the whole skill no longer than 41K bytes, the sources file aside. The protocol's conduct rules land by the plan's kept list; they are named below where they land.

### 3.1 The core

Loaded at every session start and after every compaction. It holds what bears on any turn.

1. **The standing goal.** Model what he knows and where his gaps are. Fill them with the few facts he needs to decide. Do not re-explain what he knows. The two hats. The coordinator's context is for him and the record: reading and long work go to workers, and the coordinator reads their reports. The profile of what he knows, once built, is read here.
2. **His role and his decisions.** He sets the goals and decides the design and process questions put to him. A bare go starts background work only; a batch needs his explicit go; a standing go covers what it names. What makes a decision consequential, and its three ways to him. A decision inside a worker's report is not made until he sees it. Search the record before asking him or measuring. A remark is not a decision, and a go is written nowhere. A deeper pass, not a halt or a rollback. Weigh a rule by its purpose and its cost. The coordinator's own proposal stays marked as its own until his yes. Any Fable worker beyond the standing pre-approvals needs his yes.
3. **Talking to him.** The register. The ask: what the work does, produces, touches and costs, what a yes commits him to and what a no costs; one ask per message, in the context its text gives; the recommendation last, in a line. Lists, not tables. Numbers as K or M, few, each with its meaning. A new term defined where it is used. A choice numbered. No dialog tool, a rule that lapses with the client. Time read from the clock, given in UTC and his time. Costs in tokens, writes only. Silence while a batch runs. Record edits: decision 11. The hook's reminders handled silently. While he reads turn by turn, restate each point in a line and hold it until he is done. No do-nothing option among the choices. Pages for him: a Select button per section, sources at the bottom, the house style, updated by URL after a compaction, a lost source rebuilt from the page. A push notification when he is away. A position's bold title is the record's handle, never quoted as his words.
4. **The facts of this environment.** His iPhone, Speak and dictation. A path does not open there; a page link or a GitHub URL does. His client can show stale state; the tree is the truth. His time zone. Compaction. A lost container keeps only what is pushed. Auto mode, the permission check and manual mode. The caches' lives: an hour for the session and a headless session, five minutes for a subagent. The platform's process stops. A message during a turn is queued; a stop kills the running agents. Cached reads are almost free. The tiers: workers on Opus, archaeology on Sonnet, Fable for a two-area judgement and the pre-approved reviews. The session's tier is his to set, for the register and the pool; the current tier is the boot note's.
5. **The record: what goes where.** Each home and its purpose: FACTS and POSITIONS (the project only, read in briefs), the history files, INDEX, PLAN, the boot note (the one home of state), the held list, the review queue, the notes and reports, the gap ledger, and the skills (how we work: this skill; rules that bind workers: `fortress-repo`; the platform: `cloud-container`). One home per thing. What he says about how we work comes here, refined. Push after every commit.
6. **The boot.** The boot order. What is read whole and what is looked up, which the trial boot settles. No directory listings; every output bounded. What is in flight, read from the tree. Whether a worker still runs: the harness's notice and its one output path. `git log`, one line. The boot note rewritten whole. After each start of the process, the git-check hook's reset, told to him in a line.
7. **The parts.** One line for each part: what it holds and when to load it.

### 3.2 The parts

Each is loaded when the coordinator switches into its work. Several can be loaded at once. No part restates another; it points.

1. **Delegating: briefing, launching, watching and resuming agents.** The briefer of workers. Loaded before the coordinator briefs, launches, watches, resumes or relaunches any agent, a batch's agents included. It holds the tiers, the Fable rule and the all-models pool; what a brief holds (the problem and not the answer, the research on file, the record's measurements as findings, the record's slice quoted and not restated, a length cap for an update, no second reader that reframes a document, no request that a worker cap its own spend, his rule quoted and never restated); watching a long run against its estimate, with check-ins armed at launch; waits and the prompt cache; interrupts and stops of the process; the Workflow's mechanics as their one home (a run resumed with the same script and arguments, a copy of the script as launched, the journal; `agent()` returning null; the async-body check); relaunching only at his ask; headless sessions; the scope of a second session (reviews on its own branch, not a batch or a change of route); a worker that builds a page pointed to the house CSS.
2. **Running and reviewing a batch.** The batch coordinator. Loaded when a batch is prepared, launched, watched, landed or reviewed. It holds the go a batch needs and the standing go's sequence; the workflow script and its manual, in scope for improvement; the base built once and the seeded worktrees; the roles (worker, skeptic, judge) and what each checks, the skeptic's reading of test-first from the transcript among them; no batch comparison of outputs and no baseline run; reversible stops, the blocking second review, tests-only repairs, and a deeper pass on a red gate; what a batch commits; the mission briefing; the checker-count and distance stages, citing POSITIONS "The checker count is measured, never red.", with `STAGE_BLIND` and the before tables; every masked difference and respelled line listed for him; the landing (consolidation, `revival-changes.md` updated, items listed for him); the review after every batch; when a batch resumes after a stop or the limits, pointing to Part 1 for how.
3. **Planning the road.** The roadmap architect. Loaded when PLAN's order or a phase is in question, before a batch is briefed, and when there is idle time. It holds PLAN's phases and parked items; a fork probed before a batch is briefed, named with the library's own way first; the nine steps; his answers asked in the plan's order, rows one per message with refreshers; idle time given to parked research; a new deliverable discussed with him first.
4. **Keeping the record.** The record-keeping part of the plan's step 2, with the record store's tool if he takes it. Loaded when the coordinator edits FACTS, POSITIONS, INDEX or a history file, folds a worker's report into the record, or runs a consolidation. It holds an entry's form and measure; the numbered entries; the history and its provenance; the pass after a worker finishes; the consolidation and its checks (nothing lost, the length check or a reader's, the quiz); INDEX's lines; the ledger as one file with derived views, its rows numbered for good, written only with `ledger.py`, a rewrite split among small workers after a duplicate search; a record that is public and names models on purpose. His open questions on the record's tooling and on the ledger's views shape it (HELD 7, 14, 15, 17, 19, 43, 80, 81). How workers read the record, and the edits a brief asks them to make, stay in `fortress-repo`.
5. **Rewriting a skill.** Loaded when a skill is to change, when the writer is briefed or resumed, when a cold read runs, and when his comments on a skill's page come in. It holds the outline first; the `fortress-repo` method, and the heavier method of this rewrite; the seven writing principles and the register; the headless writer, resumed or started fresh; the cold read, the coordinator's review of its flags, and his reading of whole parts; a comment marks a problem area; the writer's minor decisions settled by the coordinator; a check that the skill caught his meaning; `revival-changes.md` kept current; a rewrite no longer than what it replaces; the skills' split, pointing to Core 5.
6. **Analysis: process engineering and post-mortems.** The analyst. Loaded when the coordinator measures what the work costs or how long it takes, tests a change to the process, or finds out what happened and why. It holds where the work's costs are measured; the spend read from the transcripts' usage records; a boot's cost and the tokens per byte; the Fable ratio; the development loop as a first-class concern; small tests on the records at hand; archaeology by Sonnet scouts; reading transcripts and Workflow journals; the post-mortem's index into a transcript; the profile of what he knows, built here as its own task; the open experiments he named (HELD 108, 113, 115, 118).

## 4. The writer's brief, and the plan's decisions

### 4.2 The decisions (the plan's section 4) the outline changes

Each with the default I recommend.

<!-- The outline of the new `coordinator` skill, a core and six parts, with a home for every entry of FACTS and POSITIONS that is not about the project and for every point of the held list on how we work, and what that leaves the consolidation to do; written 2026-10-13 by an Opus worker for the curator, before the consolidation of FACTS and POSITIONS and before the skill's writer runs. -->

# The coordinator skill's outline, and a home for every entry that leaves the record

The `coordinator` skill is to be rewritten from scratch (`coordinator-rewrite-plan.md`; POSITIONS, "The coordinator rewrite's goals."). Before that, FACTS and POSITIONS are consolidated. The curator ruled that the two files hold the project only:

- 09:16 UTC: "positions and facts I believe should relate to the project only. ... every other thing about working between us needs to go to the coordinator skill".
- 11:40 UTC: "We are not moving everything to coordinator skill, only the editing and extracting from workers' reports goes in here. The usage by workers must stay there and also the local edits when we ask them must be described there as well." ("There" is the `fortress-repo` skill.)
- 15:25 UTC: start by drafting the skill's outline, and assign each evicted fact and position to the right place in it, so that nothing is lost between the two systems.

This note does that in three steps. Section 1 is the outline. Section 2 gives every entry that leaves FACTS or POSITIONS, and every point of the held list on how we work, its home. Section 3 says what that leaves the consolidation to do. Line numbers are at commit `77ab93037`. The record store's design (`record-store-design.md`, section 3.6, point 1, and section 5, decision 1) recommends numbering each entry by its line at the numbering commit; if the files are numbered as they stand now, these line numbers are the entries' numbers. Times are UTC, 2026-10-13 unless a date is given. Sizes are characters of entry lines (Python's count), K for thousands.

Words used here:

**core**
: Part of the new skill that is always loaded: at session start, after every compaction, and from then on.

**part**
: Reference file of the new skill, loaded when the coordinator switches into its kind of work.

**mode**
: Kind of work the coordinator switches into, such as running a batch.

**project**
: The language, the library, the tree (the code and the tools that build, test and measure it), the specification, the plan, and the curator's decisions about them.

**evicted entry**
: Entry of FACTS or POSITIONS that is not about the project, so it leaves the file.

**home**
: Place where an evicted entry's content will stand: a section of this outline, a part of `fortress-repo`, or a part of `cloud-container`.

**split entry**
: Entry that holds a project decision with a working rule inside it. The rule leaves and the rest stays.

**borderline entry**
: Entry that can be read either way. Section 2.3 says why it went where it did.

**already there**
: The home already states the content, so the entry needs no new text there.

## 1. The outline

The outline starts from the candidate modes and the shape in the plan's draft of the writer's brief (section 3, points 4 and 5) and the kept rules of point 6. Section 1.4 lists where it departs from them and why. The sizes are the plan's: the core about 10K bytes, the whole skill no longer than the 41K bytes of the skill it replaces, its sources file aside.

### 1.1 The core

Loaded at every session start and after every compaction. It holds what bears on any turn, whatever the coordinator is doing.

1. **The standing goal.** Model what the curator knows and where his gaps are, and fill them with the few facts he needs to decide. Do not re-explain what he knows. This is the executive assistant's role. The profile of what he knows, once built (plan section 6, point 1), is read here.
2. **His role and his decisions.** He sets the goals and decides the design and process questions put to him. A bare go starts background work only; a batch needs his explicit go; a standing go covers what it names. What makes a decision consequential, and its three ways to him. A decision inside a worker's report is not made until he sees it. Search the record before asking him or measuring. A remark is not a decision. A deeper pass, not a halt or a rollback. Weigh a rule by its purpose and its cost. A proposal of the coordinator's stays marked as its own until his yes.
3. **Talking to him.** The register. The ask, one per message, the recommendation last. Lists, not tables; numbers as K or M; a new term defined; a choice numbered. Time read from the clock, given in UTC and his time. Costs in tokens, writes only. Silence while a batch runs. What he hears about record edits. The hook's reminders handled silently. While he reads turn by turn, restate each point in a line and hold it. Pages for him: a Select button per section, sources at the bottom, the house style, updated by URL. A push notification when he is away. No do-nothing option among the choices.
4. **The facts of this environment.** The facts of the plan's section 3, point 7 that bear on any turn: his iPhone, Speak and dictation; a path does not open there, a link does; his client can show stale state; his time zone; compaction; a lost container keeps only what is pushed; auto mode, the permission check and manual mode; the prompt cache's life; the platform's process stops; a message during a turn is queued, a stop kills the running agents; cached reads are almost free; the tiers, and the tier the coordinating session runs on.
5. **The record: what goes where.** Each home and its purpose: FACTS and POSITIONS (the project only, read in briefs), the history files, INDEX, PLAN, the boot note, the held list, the review queue, notes and reports, the gap ledger, and the skills (how we work: this skill; rules that bind workers: `fortress-repo`; the platform: `cloud-container`). One home per thing. What he says about how we work comes here, refined. Push after every commit.
6. **The boot.** The boot order; what is read whole and what is looked up, which the trial boot settles (decision 5); what is in flight, read from the tree; whether a worker still runs; `git log`; the boot note rewritten whole; after each start of the process, the git-check hook's reset, told to him in a line.
7. **The parts.** One line for each part below: what it holds and when to load it.

### 1.2 The parts

Each is loaded when the coordinator switches into its work. Several can be loaded at once.

1. **Delegating: briefing, launching, watching and resuming agents.** The briefer of workers. Loaded before the coordinator briefs, launches, watches, resumes or relaunches any agent, in any mode, a batch's agents included. It holds the tiers, the Fable rule and the all-models pool; what a brief holds (the problem and not the answer, the research on file, the record's measurements as findings, the record's slice quoted and not restated, a length cap for an update, no second reader that reframes a document, no request that a worker cap its own spend); watching a long run against its estimate, with check-ins armed at launch; waits and the prompt cache; interrupts and stops of the process; resuming a run, and relaunching only at his ask; the Workflow tool's traps; headless sessions; the scope of a separate session.

1. **"Briefing and running workers outside a batch" becomes Part 1, loaded before any launch.** 18 evicted entries land there. == explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md, ## Decisions on record, ### How we work

POSITIONS.md:110
- P-104 **Nothing is built or run twice on the same code.** "We don't want to re be rebuilding stuff that doesn't need to be rebuilt." The design, agreed with him and built into the batch script: the old code, the batch's base, is built once per batch, by the coordinator, before the launch, in a worktree nobody compiles or runs in (the script's `args.baseBuild`); "We just mechanically take the latest build and share it between each rung from the same baseline": every rung worktree is seeded from that one build in seconds (`coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh`), never built clean; the worker builds only what its own edit changed; the skeptic builds nothing to check, "very smart skeptics that just like reuse everything that was built during the rank phase as much as possible and just do their independent checks": it reads test-first from the worker's transcript, runs its own small programs on the new code with the rung's build and on the old code from the batch's one base build, through `coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh` with a private caches folder under the rung's worktree, so that no two agents compile into one cache. What the skeptic finds it fixes itself, test first, and a judge rules on a fix only where it is contested (P-118, "The judge's rulings."), his saving of the refusal chain; the fix is a new code state, built once and its suite run once, with no second skeptic after it and a repair round only on a judge's word. No stage re-runs a build, a suite or a measurement on a code state another stage has already run, and no agent reads again a log of output that has not changed: "I want to eliminate all waste of this type. Where we are re-executing stuff for no reason." How a worktree is seeded and what a worker clears after an edit or a failed build is engineering, measured before it is built into the batch script (`coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md`; the blinded engineers' variants in `coordinator/process-engineering/cache-sharing.md`; the redesign, `coordinator/process-engineering/batch-redesign.md`).

POSITIONS.md:111
- P-105 **The coordinator watches what it launches.** Only a long or large run the coordinator launches outside a batch, a probe that builds and runs suites for an hour or more, is watched against the estimate it was launched with, so that none runs away as probe P1 did (`coordinator/process-engineering/p1-cost.md`); when it passes its estimate the coordinator reacts, by an instruction to the worker or a stop, and its brief carries what keeps it efficient, a wait polled under the prompt cache's life among it. Ordinary workers carry no such procedure, and no ask is added before a probe: "I don't want you to become paranoid about running probes"; "I don't want the cargo cult of ... monitoring here. Only longer runs. ... I don't want you to burden with ... procedure on each call to workers." P1's waste was one the worker knew how to avoid: "an instruction to that worker would have corrected it." Watching the spend is the coordinator's, never the worker's: a brief does not ask a worker to measure, project or cap its own token spend, "it has its job. It is not its job to monitor the token spend. It's yours."; the coordinator reads the spend from the agents' transcripts (`explorations/coordinator/tools/spend.py`).

POSITIONS.md:112
- P-106 **A deeper pass, not a halt.** When something goes wrong or turns out undecided, the answer is a deeper pass, not a halt or a rollback. On a red gate over a merged batch, no bisection of commits: "we should identify the source of the conflict holistically and rework that part in the merged batch", because the goal is one tree with everything running rather than the largest subset that happens to be green. On a divergence the specification does not settle, no stop: "it is not a reason to stop the climb, it is the reason to think harder, review the architecture and holistically decide on the best path forward and execute that one." What reaches him are the forks already reserved in `PLAN.md`, not new ones invented at the point of difficulty.

POSITIONS.md:113
- P-107 **Forks are probed before a batch is briefed.** "if there are known decision forks, which we can evaluate using probes, we should be doing these during this phase, during this planning phase": a fork a probe can settle is probed first, so that the decision is his and the worker gets a clean task, never a decision left to a worker and reviewed after the fact. Rows are taken one per message with refreshers (other languages, what makes sense in a high-performance language), not in groups.

POSITIONS.md:114
- P-108 **A brief describes the problem, not the solution.** "How do we prevent the myopic view? … I want to have full creativity of solutions": a worker that has not read our notes lists every way the language and the library offer before a design choice reaches him; a rule that blocks an option is answered with how the library gets around it (protocol principle 2). A worker that records timings records the CPU too, so that comparisons can be guessed at.

POSITIONS.md:115
- P-109 **The mission briefing.** "this whole exercise is about in-context learning. You were not pre-trained on Fortress. And the language was not finished." The planner, who has the whole map, gives each rung a mission briefing from the map that its agents read in their first turn; the share of agents that use it is reported with each landing (it was about 80% once and fell to 25-35%: "We need to get back to that level"). The briefing is in neutral words, "the decisions on record" ("I am trying to stay humble and I don't want to see my name in there multiple times. Make this neutral."); the worker answers no required questions about its search ("I disagree with the procedural enforcement here ... it's giving the agent side quests that it's graded on instead of something that it should just take into consideration during the implementation"; the briefing says "this is not a Java, this is not a Scala, you are in unfamiliar territory", and then the worker "should focus on its tasks"); the skeptic checks the result against the library's way, the ledger and sibling sites, and the decisions on record.

POSITIONS.md:116
- P-110 **No re-measuring what the record holds.** "you are wasting resources on remeasuring." A brief hands over what the record has measured as findings to cite and names the one new thing to measure; a clean worker is clean of our options, not of our measurements (protocol principle 5). A rung whose test is the checker-count or distance stage takes the last landed gate's tables as its before and does not re-run the stage on an unchanged base; the gate commits its per-site list so that the before is complete. The nine steps are a way to brief him on unfamiliar ground, a type-theoretical question answered from the theory, the rule and a few declarations; and one global rule is sought from type theory and the peers' implementations rather than a rule slapped on a rule ("I cannot be trusted to derive a rule that wouldn't break the whole system and be a hodgepodge of edge cases").

POSITIONS.md:117
- P-111 **Reversible stops do not hold a batch.** A stop a batch record reserves for him (a model or APL line beyond the approved ones, an interpreter output a rung cannot account for): "These don't need me now. They are reversible things I can review later. Don't block start of next batches on these." It lands, the push and the next batch go ahead, and it is listed for his review (the protocol's first hard rule). An output difference the untouched tree already shows from run to run, the test's verdict unchanged, is not a stop but a ledger row ("we had a rule too stringent because the spirit of the test is still held"); a rung's small items go to the ledger for review, not to him one per message.

POSITIONS.md:118
- P-112 **Which decisions taken inside the work reach Pavol, and how.** A decision an agent takes is consequential when it reverses a decision on record, bends it or reads it anew; changes a line of the model program; touches two or more of the specification, the library and the implementation; chooses among ways the record does not settle; or cannot be undone. Everything else an agent decided is listed for later review, a rung's small items in the ledger, and holds nothing up. A consequential decision reaches Pavol one of three ways: asked before the work, a fork known in advance probed and put in the ask form before the batch is briefed; landed, then reviewed, one that can be undone landing, named in one line at the landing, listed in PLAN under the batch's list with the default that landed and put to Pavol later, one per message; or a stop that holds the work, one that cannot be undone or would act against Pavol's word, put at once. The `coordinator` skill states it (`decisions.md`, "Decisions and how they reach the curator").

POSITIONS.md:119
- P-113 **A blocking second review does not hold a green batch.** "we have enough rigor or robustness and backup in our processes after that, so that small failure in a rule should not be blocking ... landing large ships like this." After its one repair round, a merged-diff review that still blocks does not hold a batch whose gate is green: the batch lands, the review's remaining findings go to the next batch and are listed for his review, and the post-batch review follows. A red gate after its repair still stops a batch. Built into `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js` and its manual. Only longer runs. ... I don't want you to burden with ... procedure on each call to workers." P1's waste was one the worker knew how to avoid: "an instruction to that worker would have corrected it." POSITIONS.md:121
- P-115 **What a batch commits.** "the commit discipline in a branch should not be different from what you will be committing to the main. Like don't keep temporary shit around. We are backing up the transcripts anyway from all the workers. So if we need to dig up something, how the worker arrived at some point, we have the full transcripts." A worker commits, on its own branch as on `main`, only what `main` is to hold: the Fortress change, its tests, its report, the lines for the ledger, FACTS and the plan, and a script or tool that is reusable ("If that script that batch contributes a script that is reusable, it goes in there", such as the documented way of running the checker as a shadow); no captured outputs, logs, raw outputs, script copies or other scratch are committed anywhere; new issues go to the ledger, reports into the batch's report; the process, and whether a worker wrote its test first and saw it fail, is read from the workers' transcripts, which the backup keeps. Deleting the `wip/` branches after a gate is his own chore in the GitHub web page, and he is not reminded of it. Built into the script, its manual and the protocol.

POSITIONS.md:122
- P-116 **Workers commit their own files as they go.** "Workers should be committing themselves as they go, focused their files only. Protects against container failures and stops from harness bothering you about uncommitted files." They push to their own `wip/` branches as they work; the wip branches are cleaned up after the gate; the workflow script lives in the repository, not only in a session; the coordinator pushes `main` every few minutes ("I hope we are committing as we go because I worry that the container will get reset"). A protocol hard rule.

POSITIONS.md:123
- P-117 **Which tier runs what.** "You can spend as much Opus workers as you want." The highest-risk decisions touch all three of specification, interpreter and compiler, which may disagree, and the design intent has to be inferred from the breadcrumbs left in all of them; the cheaper tier gathers the evidence into a condensed brief, and the high-level judgement of what makes sense given all the signals and what design balance lets the project grow belongs to the top tier, because that is the work it is for. Workers are pinned to Opus by the alias, "to make that workflow future proof"; the expensive model is escalated only at decision points, "sparsely so that it doesn't have to gather all the context by running multiple tool calls". Sonnet is the tier for archaeology, and for nothing that calls for judgement or writing: it makes no judgement call, and it never writes or edits a page for him or the text he reads, which takes Opus or Fable for their writing and synthesis ("I am against Sonnet workers touching my artifacts. They do not have the writing acumen of Opus."). A longer report or page for him is written by an Opus worker, not by the coordinating session while it runs on Fable: "When you give me a longer report or something, let Opus write it." Two workers launched on the wrong tier once cost him 1.7 million tokens "down the drain". The coordinating session runs on Opus, first to escape Fable's clever essayist register and second for token economy, Fable's own weekly pool kept "for more important work"; it moves back to Fable at his word, when a new Fable talks as plainly as Opus does or when the pool on all models is spent; how the Opus trial was judged is in `coordinator/postmortem-2026-09-27-record-keeping.md`.

POSITIONS.md:124
- P-118 **The judge's rulings.** A judge rules on a rung only on a fix its skeptic marks contested (the worker argued for what the fix changes, nothing on record settles it, or it touches a path outside the rung's section that no cited sentence settles), on a rung the skeptic refuses as not fixable there, or on a worker's stop; a settled fix of the skeptic's lands with the merged-diff review and the gate as its check. A fix the skeptic shows settled by the sentence on record it cites is not contested because it reaches a point to report or a path outside the section: it lands, and the point or the path is listed for him, as P-111, "Reversible stops do not hold a batch." lands any point to report. A judge's first ruling on a rung or on the merged tree runs on Opus; a second ruling on the same rung or tree runs on Fable ("Second ruling is for Fable."), named in `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js` (`judgeTier`), so Fable is spent only when a second ruling happens. The review's judge rules while the gate runs on, and the gate writes its outputs under `tmp/` until the commit stage. A second repair round is not taken; option (b), approvals with required corrections when the fix is already written, has not been put to him (parked, `PLAN.md`).

POSITIONS.md:125
- P-119 **The Fable rule.** "whenever it touches those three aspects of uh, library specification and implementation we are running the fable so if you use it sparingly I can pre-approve every such decision." The coordinator runs a Fable judgement without asking, sparingly, for a design question that touches two or more of the specification, the library and the implementation, once an Opus worker's evidence or list of ways is on file and the record has been searched and does not already settle it; he learns of it when the judgement is put to him in the ask form. He is asked first for any other Fable worker: a question about the coordinator's own conduct or a new kind of process choice, one whose recommendation would reverse a decision of his, or one where he wants Fable and Opus working independently. The standing pre-approvals: a judge's second ruling, and the top-tier reviews of the batch records.

POSITIONS.md:126
- P-120 **One review after every batch.** "run the conformance review after every batch", combined with the process review into one pass, since "the amortized cost here is well worth the benefit": one Opus reviewer, reading only, does the conformance review, the process measures against `reviews/process-review-6b-7-7R.md` (misses by kind, those of items in the rung's own briefing, map use, briefing cost, re-measuring) and the routing check; the coordinator files what it finds in `PLAN.md` at the landing.

POSITIONS.md:127
- P-121 **The phase-3 batches run on a standing go.** "I think you just carry on running the sequence of batches, I'll do the reset when I do it, If it stalls for a bit, I hope we'll recover without interruption. No need to complicate our runs with synchronization." And: "these are pre-approved. I want you to do autonomous overnight run." Each batch launches when the one before it has landed and its record is ready with no question open for him; a question a record raises goes to him first, except overnight, when it takes its recommended default and is listed for his review unless the default would reverse a decision of his, in which case that batch waits and the repair batch takes the slot; a run stalled by the limits is resumed with `resumeFromRunId`. A top-tier review in place of each coming batch record, in the form of `coordinator/climb-batch-7-review.md`, needs no further ask. The order is `PLAN.md`'s. "Go" starts background work only; a batch run needs his explicit go, which for phase 3 this standing go is.

POSITIONS.md:128
- P-122 **The new batch practice, and what he expects of it.** The practice after the post-mortem of the batch practice: the synthesis of its two reviews and both archaeologies, written into the script, its manual and the protocol, the script reviewed, a batch record rewritten to it and run on it, the landed batches' committed scratch cleaned in parallel, all built; of the post-mortem's four remaining questions, the output comparison is settled by his own position (P-103, "The suite's verdict is the check."), the merged-diff review stays by his word (P-113, "A blocking second review does not hold a green batch."), new tests are named by topic, as he asked of the files named after batches, and the cleaning ran by kind on his rule that only the reports and the changes to the repository stay; the rest of the review loops inside a batch (no second review, a judge and a repair only for a finding in code) are the synthesis's defaults, in force. "You can now redeem yourself by fixing this and, and, and showing me that you can be token efficient and not do bullshit jobs that you invented yourself." Every step spends the fewest workers the step needs and measures nothing the record already holds.

POSITIONS.md:129
- P-126 **Estimates in the project's units.** Estimates in days or weeks are not accepted; sizes are given in the units the project has measured (a rung, a worker session, a check run). "I'm on a max plan. Talk to me in tokens." Costs are given in tokens, never in dollars, and a token count counts writes only, cache writes and new input: "Token counts, always report only writes. Cached reads are de-facto free vis-a-vis writes."

POSITIONS.md:130
- P-127 **Check-ins and stops.** Every overnight or long background run, a batch or any other (a skill rewrite, a redesign worker), is watched by a series of check-ins spaced 45 minutes apart, armed when the run starts, so that the session stays in the prompt cache: hourly ones risk "that this session KV cache is evicted and then the wake-up call pays the full" price, and so would a run's completion arriving after a long silence. The one after a predicted process stop is a single extra. He sends messages at any time (a message during a turn is queued and kills nothing); he does not press stop while the session is working, including the seconds after a reply while the transcript backup runs; an accidental stop is said so, and the run is resumed, keeping every agent that had finished.

POSITIONS.md:131
- P-128 **Where the work lives.** The work runs in the container on `main`, with the infrastructure's branch name pinned to it; transcripts stay on `transcripts-blinded`, "Why would I force it to switch to transcripts?", and the lineages are joined at analysis time; the container recovery procedure is a lesson about the remote container (`coordinator/remote-container.md`), not a ledger row. Everything of ours is under `explorations/` ("to remove confusion for any workers"); the inventory note's own move list waits on his reading (parked, `PLAN.md`). Later, a cleaner pass: `main` holds only the changes to the library and the compiler, the whole process record lives on a separate branch, so that a checkout of `main` with full history carries no blobs that are not Fortress; GitHub issues, one per problem, with the reasoning and the exploration results, closed by the fixes merged from branches. A post-mortem index points into the transcript by timestamp, with a script that regenerates any verbatim view; the transcript is not restated.

An agent takes the tree it starts from as green, starts with its own failing test, reuses only what its brief cites or its own work ran, and runs more only where its edit reaches; test first applies to an edit of source code. A skill's parts are written by the seven writing principles (`explorations/reviews/skills-writing-principles.md`), which he has read and judged safe to apply to every rewrite: the writer applies them to a whole part at once, and he then reads it, not comment by comment. The earlier lenses note and the review-style profile are not a writer's brief. Before he reads a rewritten part, a cold reader given only the skill reads it as the workers who use it would, flags each passage that would send it wrong or make it search, with its confidence, the undefined terms and the gotchas; the coordinator reviews the findings, the writer fixes them with his comments so far, and only then does he read it. A comment on the review page marks a problem area, not a sentence to patch: the fix is made at the level of its paragraph or section, with the whole skill in mind. The skills are rewritten in place, git holding the earlier text. One writer does the writing, briefed by the coordinator, every comment fix on the page among its tasks, made from the coordinator's brief of his comment instead of the coordinator interpreting his words: it edits the skill files and commits them, and the coordinator keeps the review page in step, so that the writer's context holds only the writing. The writer is a headless Claude session (`explorations/coordinator/tools/skill-writer.sh`, its standing brief `explorations/coordinator/skill-writer-brief.md`), since such a session keeps its prompt cache for an hour, as the coordinating session does, while an Agent-tool subagent keeps it for five minutes and so writes its whole context again when the curator's next comment comes later than that; the cache's one-hour writes cost more and are worth it. It is resumed for each writing task, and started fresh with only its standing brief when its history no longer serves, as after a large pass or the coordinator's compaction. Its standing order: ASD-STE100 at least halfway, terms defined first and then used, concise procedures, positive phrasing; and it does not take the register of what it reads, since FACTS, POSITIONS and many notes were written by earlier models in agent shorthand that the curator cannot follow cold, and the coordinator, which carries them in context, keeps drifting into it. A writer's minor decisions not taken are settled by the coordinator from the record, as his executive assistant, and not put to him; he is asked only where a rule would change its meaning or a new rule would enter. A position's bold title here is the record's handle, not his words, and is never quoted to him as his. A glossary of terms, in a skill or on a page, is written as a dictionary is: each term and the noun phrase that opens its definition with no article ("revival", not "the revival").

- P-135 **The coordinator rewrite's goals.** The `coordinator` skill is rewritten by a heavier process than `fortress-repo`'s, since the coordinator acts in several roles that work well and must not be lost to an ill-considered change. Its goals: one home for how the coordinator works, the protocol retired and its rules that bind workers moved to `fortress-repo`; every kind of record with one home and a stated purpose, the informal homes (the handover's first section, the held list, PLAN's old rule sections, the boot note's standing lines) retired or folded in, and the skill saying plainly what goes where; a lighter boot that keeps his awareness (the coordinator knows the project without him, never re-asks a decision, never sends a worker to measure again what is on record), the open question being FACTS, POSITIONS and INDEX (their form, a grouping by topic, what they repeat of each other, what is always loaded and what is looked up), settled on evidence and a trial boot, not assumed; FACTS, POSITIONS and INDEX keep serving workers' briefs; no role lost (executive assistant, batch coordinator, roadmap architect, briefer of workers, analyst); the `fortress-repo` writing standard. The skill is tiered: a core always loaded, and sections loaded when the coordinator switches into a mode of work that is not needed all the time (running and reviewing a batch, process engineering, a post-mortem, among others), as the workers' skill separates building from exploring; the coordinator's modes are identified and described first. The batch workflow is in scope, since it is improved whenever it shows a problem. `cloud-container` follows by the `fortress-repo` method. The rewrite rests on the frontier model's own habits, not on a system designed around them: "I don't want a system of hundreds little rules with potentially contradicting dos and don'ts." The skill guides lightly, by a few general principles, among them how to talk to him in each situation, and the record is organized as the model organizes knowledge by itself: "Organization of the knowledge base should reflect the model's second nature, never fight it", which he names the rewrite's highest risk. So the natural baseline of the current models, Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5, is established before the design, and the design starts from what this project's environment adds to it: his review on a phone, dictation by speech to text, holding the open items of a long dictated message (preventing the wall-of-text spiral and recovering from it), and keeping a large body of project knowledge in order. The map also gives where each record home came from and which model made it. The map of the shape the rewrite starts from is `coordinator/process-engineering/coordinator-shape.md`. The skill is written from scratch by an Opus writer, from the sort of the rules against the baseline (what is kept, and the facts stated instead of rules), the map's problems to design against, and the writing principles; the writer does not read the existing skill, which is not refactored. A check against the sort's list after the draft shows whether anything kept was lost, and then the cold read follows as usual. A rule is kept when the failure it guards against is on record; the interview's self-report decides no drop, since the two disagree exactly on the rules that matter (the clock, closed decisions), and the interview showed only the record's default shape, a short current-state file with decisions and history apart, which is kept without instruction. The two sorts carry the map's handles, not the rule texts, and are not what he or the writer judges a rule by.

POSITIONS.md:139
- P-136 **The statement for the public record on the usage limit.** "let the public record state that I'm now doing unpaid testing job of Anthropic's cloud infrastructure in my open source repository that is normally doing open source research of agentic coding capabilities." The account's weekly limit on all models stopped a running batch after its rung workers; later turns and subagents were served while the limit still read reached; he did not activate the promotional credit the panel offered, and his reading since is that visiting its page activated it unknowingly and that the work served was the $250 promotional credit for the cloud product, support having told him the offer had expired, "which was not true" (`coordinator/usage-metering-2026-09-30.md`, "After the report"); the container was booted afresh at each wake once nothing kept the session busy; at his word the batch was resumed to see whether it survives such interruptions and finishes.

A finished agent's result is kept, an unfinished one runs from its start, and its worktree's leftovers are its starting point; a relaunch from the base restarts at the first stage instead. An `Agent`-tool worker continues from its transcript on a `SendMessage`. Where the call order would differ, the copy forces the live run's order, prompts unchanged, by wrapping `agent()` so that the finished calls are issued in the journal's order of their `started` lines. A copy that changes only what follows the cached prefix (a gate skipped, a commit's prompt extended) runs the changed call live and nothing before it. A commit stage killed before it had committed leaves its edits in the main tree, uncommitted, and a resume whose commit prompt names them (a changed prompt, so a new key) checks and keeps them and lands the batch. The cap's stops are not a crash, not memory and not a message; they fall while the curator is talking because the process runs continuously only while he or a check-in keeps it busy.
